title: Webpack
description: Configure Webpack entry points, loaders, plugins, code splitting, and caching — and know when it is still the right tool.

data.text: Webpack builds a dependency graph from an entry file and emits bundles. It is configuration-heavy compared with Vite, but its loader/plugin ecosystem and Module Federation support still make it the choice for large, custom enterprise builds.

data.title: What a Webpack config describes
items: **Entry** — the file where graph construction starts.
**Output** — where emitted files go and how they are named.
**Loaders** — per-file transformations (TypeScript, CSS, images) applied before bundling.
**Plugins** — build-wide hooks (HTML generation, environment variables, asset copying).

data.title: The regex needs escaping
data.text: `test: /.css$/` matches any character followed by "css" — it works by accident but also matches `mycss`. Always write `/\.css$/` in a JavaScript config file.

data.title: Run the dev server and inspect the bundle
data.code:
npm install -D webpack webpack-cli webpack-dev-server ts-loader html-webpack-plugin
npx webpack serve --mode development
npx webpack --mode production --profile   # find slow modules

data.text: `splitChunks` extracts vendor code so application changes do not invalidate the vendor bundle. `[contenthash]` in the filename changes only when file content changes, which lets browsers cache aggressively. Dynamic `import()` creates a separate chunk on demand.

Webpack build pipeline
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Entry file] --> B[Build dependency graph]
    B --> C[Loaders transform files]
    C --> D[Plugins run build hooks]
    D --> E[splitChunks]
    E --> F[Emit hashed bundles]

terms.definition: A module transformation such as ts-loader or css-loader; runs per file.
A build-wide extension that taps into Webpack lifecycle hooks.
A group of modules emitted as one output file; can be loaded lazily.
A hash of file contents used in filenames for safe long-term caching.

items.question: Is Webpack still relevant?
items.answer: Yes for large apps with bespoke build requirements, Module Federation, or legacy loader dependencies. For new apps Vite is usually faster to configure and run.

items.question: Webpack vs Vite?
items.answer: Both bundle for production, but Vite serves native ESM in development and uses Rollup for builds. Webpack bundles everything in development, which is slower but gives more control over the dev graph.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Entry, output, loaders, plugins, and mode are the core concepts.
Loaders transform individual files; plugins extend the build.
splitChunks plus contenthash gives efficient long-term caching.
Module Federation is the reason many large teams still choose Webpack.
data.takeaway: If you can explain loaders vs plugins and content hashing, you can hold a Webpack conversation.
